sheets.title: Corporate Actions
values: 92 events, chronological; refreshed 13 Oct 2026. FLAG in details = uncertain / not verified against primary source. Compiled from filings, press releases, news and broker notes.
Gojek acquires fintech firms Kartuku, Midtrans and Mapan

Pre-merger Gojek bought three Indonesian fintech companies (Kartuku, Midtrans, Mapan) to build out its payments business. Price not disclosed. Included because Midtrans (PT Midtrans, 99.99% owned, received an IDR 28.5bn intra-group capital injection from GoPay entity PT Dompet Karya Anak Bangsa on 25 May 2022) and Mapan (PT Mapan Global Tech, d/b/a Findaya, >=99% owned, the GoTo Financial entity that bought MAB shares in Apr 2024) are still GoTo Financial subsidiaries. Kartuku's current status not verified (FLAG).
Gojek buys ~4.3% stake in taxi operator Blue Bird (BIRD)

Gojek bought 108.21m BIRD shares at IDR 3,800 (~IDR 411.15bn) on 13 Feb 2020. At 14 Dec 2022 the stake was worth ~IDR 166.1bn (unrealised loss ~IDR 295bn). Still held: IDX data for holders above 1% at 31 Mar 2026 show GOTO with ~108.20m shares (4.32%). Controlling holder Pusaka Citra Djokosoetono has 28.37%.

Gojek notified KPPU of the Moka acquisition by 9 Apr 2020. Value ~US$130m (~IDR 2tn) per a Bloomberg source; earlier reports said ~US$120m. Stake acquired not stated. Included because Moka is still part of GoTo Financial's merchant business; current legal ownership % not verified from filings (FLAG).
Telkomsel invests in Gojek (US$150m convertible bond 2020; US$300m 2021)

Telkomsel (JV of Telkom Indonesia and Singtel) invested US$150m in Gojek convertible bonds in 2020 and US$300m in 2021 (total ~US$450m). Later reported as ~23.72bn GOTO shares (~1.99%) at an average acquisition price of ~IDR 270/share (~IDR 6.40tn). Exact month dates not verified from primary filings (FLAG).
Gojek (via GoPay entity PT Dompet Karya Anak Bangsa) raises Bank Jago (ARTO) stake from 4.14% to 22.16%

PT Dompet Karya Anak Bangsa (DKAB, the GoPay entity) bought 1,956,600,000 ARTO shares at IDR 1,150 (~IDR 2.25tn), taking its holding from 449.14m shares (4.14%) to ~2.4bn shares (22.16%). Stated purpose: investment and a long-term partnership on financial inclusion (Bank Jago accounts in the Gojek app). Control did not change: PT Metamorfosis Ekosistem Indonesia (MEI) and Wealth Track Technology (WTT) kept a combined 51%. Pre-merger deal, included because the stake is still held (see 2021-03-17).
Strategic equity investment (associate - Bank Jago) / rights issue participation
GoPay (DKAB) takes up most of its rights in Bank Jago's ~IDR 7tn rights issue; stake ~21.4%

ARTO rights issue (up to 3bn new shares at IDR 2,350) ended 17 Mar 2021; shares outstanding rose from 10,856,250,000 to 13,745,773,441. DKAB took up 560m of its 664.8m rights (~IDR 1.31-1.32tn) and ended with ~2.96bn shares (21.44%). GIC entered with 8.08%. Later holdings: 2,965,745,000 shares (21.4%) at Dec 2022; ~21.4% in an Apr 2026 report (MEI ~29.79%, WTT ~11.68%, GIC ~8.28%, free float ~27%). No evidence found of a second ARTO rights issue in 2022 or of later GoTo purchases or sales of ARTO shares (FLAG). The Kontan source is internally inconsistent on the pre-rights % (22.16% vs 20.48%).
Gojek affiliate PT Pradipa Darpa Bangsa buys 4.76% of Matahari Putra Prima (MPPA, Hypermart)

PT Multipolar Tbk (MLPL) sold 896,327,200 MPPA shares (11.9%) on 6 Apr 2021. Buyers: PT Pradipa Darpa Bangsa (Gojek group) 358,530,900 shares (4.76%), Panbridge Investment Ltd 3.33% and Theadmore Capital Ltd 3.81%. Price not disclosed.
Gojek and Tokopedia announce merger to form GoTo Group

Gojek and Tokopedia announced their merger into GoTo (name also a nod to 'gotong royong'), after Gojek-Grab talks in early 2021 reached an impasse. At formation GoTo cited ~100m monthly active users, >11m merchants and >2m drivers; GoTo Financial set up around the same time.
Gojek Thailand sold to AirAsia (all-share deal, ~US$50m)

AirAsia SuperApp / AirAsia Digital acquired Gojek's Thailand operations in an all-share transaction reported at ~US$50m; Gojek received an equity stake in AirAsia's digital business. Deal announced ~early July 2021 (Rajah & Tann deal note dated 7 Jul 2021).
GoTo buys a further 6.74% of MPPA from Multipolar for IDR 355bn; standby buyer in MPPA rights issue

PT Aplikasi Karya Anak Bangsa (GoTo) bought 507,142,900 MPPA shares (6.74%) from MLPL at IDR 700/share (IDR 355bn) in a crossing on 4 Oct 2021. Kontan's headline says total ownership rose to 11.5%. GoTo was also named standby buyer in MPPA's Q4 2021 rights issue (up to 1,171,200,788 shares / IDR 890.11bn); the projected stake afterwards was ~5.49-6.20%. Later sources list only 507.14m shares (~6%, unchanged since purchase) at Dec 2022, with an unrealised loss of ~IDR 278bn, and 5.98% before MPPA's Jul 2023 rights issue. Sources do not explain why the 4.76% Pradipa stake is missing from those figures, and GoTo's current MPPA holding is unverified (FLAG).

MLPL's controlling holder PT Inti Anugerah Pratama sold 1.66bn MLPL shares (11.37%). GoTo VP Business Development Stefan Ko said GoTo 'officially owns 4.8%' of MLPL. The article cites a 79.87m-share purchase by GoTo and a transaction value of IDR 805.75bn (meta description). These figures do not reconcile with a 4.8% stake (FLAG). Price per share not disclosed. Not listed among GoTo's listed holdings (ARTO, MPPA, BIRD) in a Dec 2022 Kontan review, so the current status is unknown (FLAG).
GoTo buys out foreign minority investors in GoPay to become sole owner

Ahead of the IPO, GoTo bought the GoPay stakes held by Facebook, Google, PayPal, Tencent Mobility and Gamvest; the sellers were to reinvest the proceeds in GoTo. Stake size and price are behind a paywall (FLAG). GoPay entities are now ~99.99% owned (e.g., DKAB per 2022-2025 sources).
Report that GoTo planned to buy a majority of BFI Finance (BFIN) via tender offer

Kontan cited an unnamed source saying GoTo would buy a majority of PT BFI Finance Indonesia Tbk via a tender offer. BFIN's director gave a non-committal response. No GoTo deal followed. A Kontan headline (not read) says a 2022 BFIN tender offer was completed by Trinugraha Capital & Co (48.15%) (FLAG). BFIN reappears in the Jul 2026 Bank Jago merger rumour (existing log).
GoTo raises >US$1.3bn in first close of pre-IPO round

Led by Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA); participants included Avanda, Fidelity International, Google, Permodalan Nasional Berhad, Primavera Capital, SeaTown, Temasek, Tencent and Ward Ferry. Media estimated valuation at US$28.5-30bn (GoTo declined to comment).
Gojek and TBS Energi Utama (TOBA) form 50/50 EV JV Electrum (PT Energi Kreasi Bersama)

Announced Nov 2021 with an initial US$10m commitment and potential investment of up to US$1bn over five years (TBS's Pandu Sjahrir). Scope: two-wheel EV manufacturing, battery packs, battery-swap infrastructure and EV financing. PT Energi Kreasi Bersama (EKB) was legalised by the Ministry of Law (AHU) on 9 Dec 2021 with authorised/issued/paid-up capital of IDR 71.75bn. Shareholders: GoTo via PT Rekan Anak Bangsa (RAB) and TOBA via PT Karya Baru TBS. Ownership was 50/50: RAB held 50% (38,875 shares in Jul 2022; 78,500 shares in Nov 2023, with PT Karya Baru TBS holding 78,500). Cikarang factory groundbreaking 23 Jun 2023. In Nov 2023 TOBA committed IDR 300bn from its 2023 capex, and Electrum planned >IDR 1tn of investment (R&D, factory, battery-swap stations). No matching GoTo equity amount was found. Latest: H1 2026 revenue US$9.1m (+184% YoY), segment EBITDA +US$0.5m. GoTo's FY2025 investment in joint ventures was IDR 503.1bn (all JVs). Whether the 50/50 split still holds after 2023 is not verified (FLAG).
Sale of Alfamart stake (~IDR 1.5tn) and Coins.ph divestment

GoTo sold its Alfamart (AMRT) stake for ~IDR 1.5tn in late 2022 (share count/price undisclosed). Coins.ph (acquired by Gojek Jan 2019 for US$72m) was divested in 2022 (Wikipedia cites US$200m to Wei Zhou; FLAG - not verified against primary source).
Electrum, Pertamina, Gogoro and Gesits expand two-wheel EV and battery-swap collaboration

Expanded the South Jakarta commercial EV trial to thousands of units in 2022, with Gojek drivers operating them. Electrum is the integrator/developer, Pertamina Patra Niaga provides gas stations for battery swapping, and Gogoro and Gesits provide vehicles and swap technology. No equity or investment amounts disclosed. A Kontan headline says Pertamina Patra Niaga also partnered with Gojek/TBS on battery-swap/charging stations (SPBKLU); details not read (FLAG).
IPO prospectus dividend policy: no dividends until accumulated retained earnings are positive

GoTo intends to pay dividends only after it has positive accumulated retained earnings (negative at 31 Jul 2021). Payments require AGM approval on the Board of Directors' recommendation, depend on earnings, cash flow and prospects, and may be restricted by financing agreements. No payout ratio was stated. Series A and B shares carry equal dividend rights. GoTo has paid no dividend to date. No source found on any dividend plan after the first quarterly net profit in Q1 2026 (GAP).
GoTo lists on IDX Main Board (ticker GOTO) at IDR 338/share

46.7bn Series A shares offered (new shares plus treasury shares for over-allotment). Total raised ~US$1.1bn (IDR 15.8tn): US$954.7m (IDR 13.7tn) offering proceeds + US$146.3m (IDR 2.1tn) from treasury shares sold for over-allotment. Market cap ~US$28bn (IDR 400.3tn) at listing. Day-one close IDR 388 (~+14.8%).
AGM approves private placement authority of up to 10% (~118.44bn Series A shares); lapsed unused

AGM approved a non-pre-emptive capital increase (PMTHMETD) of up to 10% of issued capital (up to ~118bn Series A shares at IDR 1 par; max dilution 9.09%), valid for one year (POJK rule cited in source). Stated use: working capital for Tokopedia, Dompet Anak Bangsa and/or Multifinance Anak Bangsa. GoTo did not use it (management said in Jun 2023 it had no plan to). In Dec 2022 GoTo told a public expose it was exploring a private placement as the lock-up expired.
Asset transfer to JV (Electrum) / affiliated transaction
GoTo subsidiary PT Rekan Anak Bangsa sells e-motorbike assets to Electrum for IDR 23.6bn
RAB sold 251 Gogoro 2 Plus smart scooters, 502 battery kits and trademark assets to PT Energi Kreasi Bersama (Electrum), in which RAB held 50%, for IDR 23.6bn (agreement 29 Jul 2022).
Bank Jago named strategic funding partner for GoPayLater Cicil on Tokopedia

Bank Jago is a strategic partner funding GoPayLater Cicil (1-12-month instalments on Tokopedia). Structure (channelling vs joint financing) and volumes not disclosed. GoPayLater is provided by PT Multifinance Anak Bangsa (MAB). No source found for other bank lending or channelling partners (e.g., BNI, Mandiri, BCA) or for any securitisation (GAP).
GoTo (via GoPay entity DKAB) acquires 100% of PT Kripto Maksima Koin for IDR 124.83bn

DKAB (99.99% owned by GoTo) bought 100% of crypto asset trader PT Kripto Maksima Koin (KMK; Bappebti registration dated 28 Jan 2022) from two unaffiliated individuals (50,000 shares) for ~IDR 124.83bn (~US$8.4m). Purpose: business expansion. Divested/deconsolidated in 2024 (see 2024-10).
Planned convertible bond (up to US$1bn, later US$500m) explored, then cancelled

Sep 2022 (IFR): GoTo was considering a convertible bond of up to US$1bn, with an indicative 5-year tenor and 3-5% coupon. Apr 2023 (Bloomberg via Bisnis/IBP): the plan, cut to US$500m (~IDR 7.42tn), was dropped after talks with BlackRock, PAG and IFC. Reasons: avoid mixed signals to investors and smaller funding needs (cash ~IDR 29tn said to be enough to reach positive operating cash flow). GoTo did not confirm. Later replaced by the smaller IFC/Franke deal (2023-10-03).
GoTo entered a bank facility in November 2022; IDR 467bn was outstanding as of June 2025 and was refinanced by the Sept 2025 DBS/UOB facility. Lenders/size of the 2022 facility not verified (FLAG).
GoTo lays off ~1,300 employees (~12% of workforce)
Cost-cutting amid expected prolonged macro uncertainty; cuts across four countries.
8-month pre-IPO lock-up expires; planned controlled placement abandoned

Lock-up on major holders (incl. Alibaba, SoftBank) expired 30 Nov 2022, freeing ~1 trillion shares (>90% of outstanding) for sale. A planned controlled placement to manage the overhang did not proceed (no agreement on price; buyers sought up to 30% discount). Shares fell to record lows.
GoTo lays off ~600 more employees (cumulative ~1,900 with the Nov 2022 round)

About 600 roles affected across the ecosystem: two GoTo Financial offline merchant teams merged, Mitra Tokopedia partly scaled back, recruitment team restructured, and non-core initiatives cut or delayed. Bisnis reports ~1,900 total layoffs including Nov 2022.
SoftBank (SVF GT Subco) and other early backers gradually sell GOTO shares

Multiple IDX disclosures in 2023-early 2024 of SoftBank's SVF GT Subco selling GOTO tranches (e.g., ~200m shares May 2023, ~133.9m Jan 2024), alongside GPF. SoftBank nonetheless still held 7.65% as of May 2025 and Sept 2026 lists. Individual tranche details not fully compiled (FLAG).
Argor Capital (formerly Go-Ventures, GoTo's CVC arm) launches US$240m Fund 2 with GoTo as LP

Go-Ventures, GoTo's corporate venture arm, was rebranded Argor Capital and launched a US$240m second fund. GoTo is an LP alongside sovereign wealth funds, institutions, corporates and family offices; the fund makes investment decisions independently. GoTo's commitment not disclosed (FLAG).
2023 AGM/EGM: Patrick Walujo becomes CEO; Andre Soelistyo moves to Board of Commissioners

Announced 8 June 2023. Andre Soelistyo (President Director & Group CEO) moved to Deputy Chairman of the Board of Commissioners; Patrick Walujo (Northstar co-founder) nominated President Director & Group CEO; Thomas Husted Vice President Director & COO; Agus D.W. Martowardojo President Commissioner; Garibaldi Thohir Commissioner. AGM also renewed authority for share ownership program issuance and approved a non-pre-emptive capital increase (PMTHMETD) capped at 10% of issued capital; EGM approved Series A/B share conversions.
AGM/EGM renews private placement authority (up to 118,436,392,950 Series A shares)

The 2023 AGM/EGM approved a new non-pre-emptive capital increase authority of up to 118,436,392,950 new Series A shares (10%), to grow the business and strengthen capital. Partly used in Oct 2023 (17.05bn shares to Bhinneka Holdings, see 2023-10-03).
GoTo sold entertainment/streaming unit GoPlay to Edy Sulistyo (founder/ex-CEO of Loket.com); value undisclosed.
US$150m IFC/Franke package: 17.05bn new shares to Bhinneka Holdings, US$50m notes, and US$150m exchangeable bonds (EXPLAINS FY2023 'equity-linked bond proceeds')

Structure: (1) GoTo issued 17,045,733,334 new Series A shares (~1.42%) at IDR 90 (~IDR 1.53tn / ~US$100m) to Bhinneka Holdings (22) Limited (BHL, Cayman), using the June 2023 PMTHMETD authority. (2) GoTo International Finance (22) Limited (100% GoTo) issued US$50m notes to BHL, guaranteed by GOTO (Notes Subscription Agreement 2 Oct 2023; Citibank N.A. Hong Kong custodian). (3) BHL funded both by issuing US$150m equity-linked bonds: IFC US$125m, WAF Investments Cayman LLC (Franke & Co) US$25m. Terms: 5% coupon paid semi-annually, maturity Oct 2028, exchangeable into the GOTO Series A shares held by BHL at IDR 135/share (50% premium to the 1-month VWAP to 2 Oct 2023). Placing agents: Citigroup Global Markets and Goldman Sachs (Singapore). Total ~IDR 2.3tn. Placement proceeds: 25% GoTo, 15% each to Tokopedia, Swift Logistic Solutions, Dompet Anak Bangsa, Multifinance Anak Bangsa and GoTo Solusi Niaga (sources disagree slightly on the list). GoTo's FY2025 accounts consolidate BHL as an entity with no effective ownership (total assets IDR 2.92tn at end-2025). This is very likely why the bonds appear as 'equity-linked bond proceeds' (~IDR 2.3tn) in GoTo's FY2023 cash flow statement. That link is our inference, not stated in a source read (FLAG). IFC also to support fleet EV transition. Outstanding/exchanged amounts as of 2026 not found (GAP).
completed; bonds outstanding to Oct 2028 (exchange status unknown)
GoPay and Bank Jago launch 'GoPay Tabungan by Jago' bank account

A Bank Jago savings/transaction account inside the GoPay and Gojek apps: GoPay balance converts in ~2 minutes, 2.5% p.a. interest, no monthly fee or minimum balance, LPS-insured. Announced by Hans Patuwo (then President, Fintech). Commercial partnership with a ~21.4% associate.
IDX denies circulating notice that GOTO would do a reverse stock split
A fake notice dated 7 Nov 2023 claimed a GOTO reverse split to IDR 450 par. IDX Director Irvan Susandy called it untrue (unsigned by the named IDX officials).
GoTo subsidiary PT Rekan Anak Bangsa grants Electrum a loan facility of up to IDR 45bn

RAB lends EKB (Electrum) up to IDR 45bn at 10.95% p.a. on the unpaid principal, repayable in full within 5 years of the facility agreement, for opex and capex (including subsidiaries' capex via equity injections). At the time RAB and PT Karya Baru TBS each held 78,500 EKB shares (50/50). Drawn amount not found (GAP).
TikTok to acquire 75.01% of Tokopedia; GoTo retains 24.99%

Announced 11 Dec 2023. TikTok to take 75.01% controlling stake in PT Tokopedia (merged with TikTok Shop Indonesia) and commit >US$1.5bn of long-term funding. GoTo keeps 24.99%, stated at the time to be non-dilutive going forward. GOTO shares fell sharply on announcement.

Tokopedia issued ~38.19m new shares (75.01%) to TikTok for US$840m; TikTok also provided a US$1bn promissory note to Tokopedia (working capital) and acquired ~US$340m of Tokopedia business assets/contracts. Purchase price IDR 747.87/share vs. pre-deal valuation of 100% of Tokopedia at US$606m (IDR 9.4tn). GoTo deconsolidated Tokopedia, retaining 24.99%, and booked ~IDR 80.3tn non-cash goodwill impairment/loss. GoTo receives quarterly e-commerce service fees based on a sliding percentage of Tokopedia GMV. Put/call option terms NOT found in sources reviewed (GAP). No evidence found of a later sale of GoTo's remaining 24.99%.
Bloomberg reports Grab and GoTo revived merger talks
Bloomberg (Fri 9 Feb 2024) reported preliminary revival of ride-hailing merger talks. GoTo denied on Tue 13 Feb 2024 that it was in any discussion, citing positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2023.
M&A (minority buyout) / affiliated transaction - GoTo Financial multifinance
GoTo (via PT Mapan Global Tech) buys 11.04% of PT Multifinance Anak Bangsa (GoPayLater) from commissioner Winato Kartono

PT Mapan Global Tech (Findaya; >=99% GoTo) bought 309.12m MAB shares (11.04%) from Winato Kartono, a GoTo commissioner (appointed Mar 2023) and Provident co-founder, for IDR 32,452,859,608 (nominal value IDR 30.91bn); deed signed 1 Apr 2024. GoTo's ownership (previously 85% via PT Gofin Karya Anak Bangsa) rose to ~96.04% (DealStreetAsia says 96.4%). GoTo also planned to inject IDR 678.72bn of IPO proceeds into MAB (not yet disbursed as of the Jan 2024 use-of-proceeds report). How MAB was originally acquired or set up was not found (GAP).
GoTo Logistics (PT Paket Anak Bangsa) divested

GoTo sold 2.43m shares of PT Paket Anak Bangsa (parent of GoTo Logistics; subsidiaries PT Swift Shipment Solutions and PT Swift Logistics Solutions) to third parties for IDR 14.7bn, losing control. Rationale: internal restructuring after Tokopedia deconsolidation.

Per June 2024 financial statements, GoTo repurchased 3,825,000,000 Series A shares for IDR 198.40bn (~0.32% of shares; implied ~IDR 52/share per CNBC estimate). Executed in June 2024 under the US$200m authorization (these shares are included in the 32.19bn cumulative total). FLAG: one source treats it as a separate pre-AGM phase.
AGM/EGM approves up to US$200m (~IDR 3.2tn) buyback (12 Jun 2024 - 11 Jun 2025)
Shareholders approved market buyback of up to US$200m (~IDR 3.2-3.26tn) for 12 months, plus changes to board composition.
Share class (Series B multiple voting shares)
EGM approves CEO Patrick Walujo as an eligible holder of Series B multiple-voting shares

Under POJK 22/2021, the EGM approved Patrick Walujo as a party that may hold Series B (MVS) shares. Management said this would not increase the number of Series B shares. GoTo no longer issues founder Series B shares, so any transfer would come from existing holders and converts to Series A unless made to an approved MVS holder. Series B carries ~30x votes (CNBC Indonesia). At listing, the founders plus PT Saham Anak Bangsa held 6.08% of shares and 58.26% of votes. Named Series B holders in 2024: William Tanuwijaya, Melissa Siska Juminto, Andre Soelistyo, Kevin Aluwi and PT Saham Anak Bangsa. Whether Walujo actually received Series B shares, and the Series B position after his Dec 2025 exit, were not found (GAP).
GoPay Later launched on TikTok's ShopTokopedia

GoTo Financial's BNPL (credit limit up to IDR 10m; 1/3/6/12-month tenors) became available on ShopTokopedia (TikTok), extending the GoTo-TikTok partnership in which GoPay was already a payment method. (The quarterly GMV-based e-commerce service fee from Tokopedia, effective 1 Feb 2024, is already in the existing log.)
Treasury share cancellation / capital reduction; C-suite
EGM approves cancellation of 10.26bn treasury shares; Simon Ho appointed CFO

Capital reduction via cancellation of 10.26bn Series A treasury shares (~0.85% of outstanding) originating from pre-IPO buybacks (2021) and the IPO greenshoe/stabilisation (2022). Post-cancellation ~1.19 trillion shares listed (~1.14tn Series A, ~50.57bn Series B per KB Valbury; source states 'billion', likely a typo). Jacky Lo resigned as director/CFO; Simon Tak Leung Ho (ex-Maya, FinVolution) appointed director and Group CFO.
GoTo announced exit from Vietnam to focus on Indonesia/Singapore and profitability; services terminated from 16 Sep 2024.
GoTo loses control of Kripto Maksima Koin (now FLOQ); remaining stake becomes an associate

GoTo's effective stake in KMK fell from 99.99% (2023) to 67.96% during 2024. After GoTo divested an interest in a subsidiary in Oct 2024, KMK and its holding company Kripto Maksima Holding (KMH) were deconsolidated. The retained interest was remeasured at fair value and is now equity-accounted. KMK was rebranded FLOQ (grand launch 30 May 2025) under Timothy Ronald (Akademi Crypto), with ex-Tokocrypto CEO Yudhono Rawis involved. Buyer, price and GoTo's residual % were not disclosed or confirmed (FLAG). GoTo's Pablo Malay has been a KMH director since 2024.
GoTo raises effective ownership of PT Multifinance Anak Bangsa from 96.03% to 99.99%

GoTo's FY2025 consolidated financial statements show MAB's effective ownership up from 96.03% (2024) to 99.99% (2025) ('the Group added its ownership in the subsidiary'). The FY2025 cash flow statement shows IDR 45.6bn paid to acquire non-controlling interests, but it is not confirmed that this payment relates only to MAB. The FY2025 statements also list two new subsidiaries set up in 2025: Velox Cloud Holdings Pte. Ltd. (100%) and GoTo Times (Beijing) Technology Co., Ltd. (99.99%). Counterparty (presumably Winato Kartono's remaining ~3.96%) and price not found (FLAG).
Reuters: Grab and GoTo in advanced merger talks

Talks resumed Dec 2024; investors eager for a 2025 deal; combined value ~US$25bn. Both declined to comment; GoTo subsequently called reports speculation. Reports (Bloomberg, Feb 2025) cited Grab considering valuation >US$7bn, e.g. all-stock at ~IDR 100/share (later reporting also cited IDR 100-110).
Reports GoTo exploring sale/spin-off of GoTo Financial; Grab due diligence under way

DealStreetAsia-sourced reports: GoTo in advanced talks to sell GoTo Financial (GoPay, GoPay Later) to a Japanese investor; Grab reportedly began due diligence on GoTo via a Big Four firm (4-6 months). No transaction confirmed (FLAG: unconfirmed).
Reuters: Grab aims to sign GoTo takeover in Q2 2025 (~US$7bn)

Grab hired advisers and was in talks with banks for financing; structure reportedly: GoTo sells international unit and all Indonesian operations except its financial-services arm to Grab. GoTo (8 May and 16 May 2025 filings) said it had received confidential, non-binding, early-stage offers from several parties, no agreement or decision.
Grab says it is not in talks with GoTo 'at this time'

Grab statement: 'The parties are not involved in any discussions at this time and Grab has not entered into any definitive agreements.' Momentum stalled amid KPPU/regulatory concerns; Reuters (19 Jun 2025) reported government conditions (driver fees/bonuses, Indonesian majority ownership per DPR deputy speaker Dasco).
Cumulative 32,186,417,803 Series A shares (~2.99%) repurchased for ~US$130.83m / IDR 2.09tn vs. US$200m cap (implied ~IDR 65/share). Completion disclosed 16 Jun 2025. Shares held in treasury.
AGM/EGM approves new US$200m (~IDR 3.3tn) buyback (19 Jun 2025 - 18 Jun 2026), treasury-to-MESOP transfer and board changes

Proposed 13 May 2025. Approved buyback up to US$200m (~IDR 3.3tn), max 10% of capital, on/off exchange, funded by internal cash. Approved transfer of treasury shares (from 2024-25 buyback) to employee/management stock ownership program (later reversed, see 2026-07-28). Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo became Deputy CEO/Vice President Director replacing Thomas Husted; new directors incl. Monica Lynn Mulyanto (CPO), R.A. Koesoemohadiani (Legal/Corp Sec), Ade Mulyana, Wuzhen (William) Xiong (CTO), Sudhanshu Raheja (President, GoTo Financial). Execution: 7.59bn shares repurchased 19 Jun 2025 - 18 Jun 2026 (value not found - GAP).
DealStreetAsia: Grab-GoTo merger talks called off again
Sources said talks had ended once again.
IDR 4.65tn (~US$280m) 4-year term loan from DBS Indonesia and UOB

Mandated lead arrangers PT Bank DBS Indonesia and UOB. Proceeds partly to refinance Nov 2022 facility (IDR 467bn outstanding at Jun 2025); remainder for general corporate purposes incl. investments and working capital.
Government signals support for Grab-GoTo combination; Danantara golden share discussed

Palace spokesperson said government discussed a possible merger/acquisition (~7 Nov). Reuters (13 Nov) reported government now fully supports a deal after earlier opposition; Danantara in talks to take a 'golden share' (veto rights) in combined entity; Anthony Tan met President Prabowo. State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi linked the talks to drafting of the ride-hailing Presidential Regulation. GoTo (10-11 Nov) said no decision/agreement with Grab or Danantara. Danantara CIO Pandu Sjahrir: decision rests with companies.
SoftBank, Provident, Peak XV push to replace CEO Patrick Walujo
Bloomberg-reported: major backers pressing for CEO change, seen as smoothing path to Grab deal (Walujo had opposed a Grab takeover).
KPPU chair warns it could cancel a GoTo-Grab merger
KPPU Chair M. Fanshurullah Asa said the merger must comply with competition law and KPPU would not hesitate to cancel it if anti-competitive; warned GoTo, Grab and Danantara against bypassing KPPU.
EGM appoints Hans Patuwo as President Director & Group CEO, replacing Patrick Walujo

Nominated 24 Nov 2025. Patuwo (ex-COO) replaced Walujo (~2.5-year tenure). Co-founder Andre Soelistyo and Santoso Kartono appointed commissioners, replacing Pablo Malay and Winato Kartono; director Ade Mulyana resigned. GoTo stated the EGM was not related to any corporate action plan.
Bloomberg: Grab-GoTo deal hits snag over Telkomsel's ~2% stake

Telkomsel (state-linked; ~2% of GoTo, ~US$450m invested 2020-21) reportedly unwilling to sell near market price due to state-loss liability concerns; separate buyout structure for Telkomsel being discussed. GoTo mkt cap ~US$4.2bn vs Grab ~US$18.5bn; prior >US$7bn / ~IDR 100/share all-stock idea outdated after ~30% share drop. Draft ride-hailing decree (commission cap, insurance) also unresolved. Negotiations ongoing; no conclusion. This is the LATEST substantive public reporting on deal negotiations found (as of 2026-10-10).

Hans Patuwo exercised 188.18m ESOP shares (holding 763.01m); Deputy CEO Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo acquired 515.89m via ESOP and sold all on 16-17 Mar 2026 at ~IDR 52. Program administered via GoTo Peopleverse Fund. Exercise price not disclosed.
GoTo reports first-ever quarterly net profit (Q1 2026: IDR 257.9bn)
FY2025 had record revenue but IDR 1.18tn net loss (reported 13 Mar 2026). H1 2026 net profit IDR 607.48bn on revenue IDR 10.99tn (+28.4% YoY).
Presidential Regulation (Perpres) No. 27/2026 caps 2-wheel ride-hailing (GoRide) commission at 8%

Announced/signed by President Prabowo on May Day 2026 (per Pluang); GOTO fell ~5-7% on 4 May. GoTo and Grab agreed (22 Jun) to cut GoRide/GrabBike commission to 8% from 1 Jul 2026. Bisnis reports formal release by State Secretariat on 8 Oct 2026, covering ride, food and goods delivery; derivative regs due Dec 2026. FLAG: signing vs. publication date inconsistent across sources. GoTo cut FY2026 on-demand EBITDA guidance by IDR 0.3tn.
Danantara discloses <1% stake in GoTo; considering increase

Danantara bought GOTO shares on-market earlier in 2026 (<1%); GoTo welcomed it in 5 May 2026 IDX letter. On 11 May, Danantara CIO Pandu Sjahrir said it may raise its stake (no level decided); CEO Rosan Roeslani said ownership would be expanded gradually.
GOTO hits IDX IDR 50 price floor and stays pinned
Per IDNFinancials first hit IDR 50 on 5 May 2026 (TechTimes says closed at floor 13 May; FLAG). Stock illiquid at floor with large sell queues through Sept 2026.
MSCI freezes GOTO index changes, warns of removal (effective 1 Jun 2026)
MSCI froze changes to GOTO's NOS/FIF/DIF and additions/deletions due to weak liquidity, with reassessment at August 2026 review. GOTO was ~2.94% of Indonesian MSCI weight (Mar 2026).
IDX moves GOTO from New Economy Board to Development Board
Part of IDX periodic board review (fundamentals, liquidity, compliance); effective 29 May 2026. BELI moved likewise.
FTSE removes GOTO from Global Equity Index Series (effective 22 Jun 2026)
Removal from FTSE Global Mid Cap Index because the IDX Development Board does not meet GEIS eligibility.
AGM/EGM approves up to IDR 3.5tn buyback (19 Jun 2026 - 18 Jun 2027); board unchanged

Proposed 11 May 2026 (cash IDR 22.7tn at Mar 2026; treasury ~3.3% at Apr 2026). Agus D.W. Martowardojo reappointed President Commissioner; Marjorie Tiu Lao (Independent) and Santoso Kartono reappointed; no BoD/BoC changes. As of Q2 call (29 Jul 2026) no repurchases executed under this program; management 'avoiding a rushed implementation'.
approved / not yet executed (as of Jul 2026)
8% commission cap takes effect for 2-wheel ride-hailing; GoTo cuts ODS guidance, raises fintech

GoTo applies the 8% platform commission (from ~20%) to 2W mobility from 1 Jul 2026 under Perpres 27/2026. FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance: ODS cut to Rp1.4-1.5tn (from 1.7-1.8tn), fintech raised to Rp1.7-1.8tn (from 1.4-1.5tn), group held at Rp3.2-3.4tn. BRIDS estimates 2W = ~10% of ODS gross revenue; UOB KH cut ODS revenue by ~3%.

BRI Danareksa Sekuritas, GOTO company update, 3 Jul 2026 (client-provided PDF)
UOB Kay Hian, Asian Gems Corporate Highlights, 28 Sep 2026 (client-provided PDF)
https://teknologi.bisnis.com/read/20260519/266/1974800/goto-ikuti-aturan-pemerintah-92-biaya-perjalanan-goride-jadi-hak-driver-gojek
Bank Jago and BFI Finance deny merger rumour

Reports of a Bank Jago (GoTo/GoPay associate, ~22% per Wikipedia) and BFI Finance merger; both denied, Bank Jago said no merger in its 2026 business plan. GoTo management on Q2 call said a merger was 'still not 100% certain'.
GoTo cancels treasury-to-MESOP plan; to pursue capital reduction instead

Dropped plan to transfer ~32.19bn treasury shares (2024-25 buyback) to the employee/management stock ownership program approved June 2025; will instead cancel them via capital reduction (~2.7% of shares). Reviewing options for a further 7.59bn treasury shares bought 19 Jun 2025 - 18 Jun 2026.
Management calls a reverse stock split 'one possible option'; still evaluating

On the Q2 2026 call, management called a reverse split 'one possible option' to address the share price but said it is not straightforward in Indonesia, has few precedents and is viewed negatively by the public. Options are still being evaluated. Bisnis (31 Jul 2026) reported GoTo weighing the risks of a reverse split to lift the stock from the IDR 50 floor. No proposal, ratio or EGM agenda found. The 14 Oct 2026 EGM agenda covers only the capital reduction and the director resignation.
MSCI removes GOTO from MSCI Indonesia (Global Standard) index, effective after close 31 Aug 2026

Removal driven by illiquidity at IDR 50 floor; weight reduced to zero ahead of deadline. GOTO ~4% of MSCI Indonesia at end-July; estimated passive outflow ~IDR 1tn (Mirae). GoTo called it 'purely technical'.
Morgan Stanley buys ~3.8bn GOTO at IDR 23 in negotiated market; crosses 5%

Morgan Stanley & Co International Plc bought 3.13bn shares at IDR 23 plus ~657m via crossing (Rp87.3bn total), 54% below the IDR 50 regular-market floor. Stake 4.82% -> 5.15% (55.57bn -> 59.36bn shares). Stated purpose: investment. Ahead of MSCI Global Standard exit (effective 31 Aug). Seller not disclosed; no mention of employees/ESOP.
Deputy President Director Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo resigns
Resignation letter received 28 Aug 2026 (personal/family reasons); subject to EGM approval on 14 Oct 2026. No successor named.
MSCI exit effective: GOTO largest net foreign sell, mostly in negotiated market at avg IDR 24

First trading day after MSCI removal. Net foreign sell Rp152.5bn across all markets, of which Rp152.3bn in the negotiated market at an average IDR 24/share (Stockbit data). Kontan reports BlackRock stake fell sharply while Vanguard accumulated (figures paywalled). Consistent with passive index funds exiting via block trades because the regular market was pinned at IDR 50.
Morgan Stanley buys ~21.9bn GOTO at IDR 25 (negotiated market); stake to 7.59%

Three trades on 2 Sep: 12.57bn, ~200m and 9.22bn shares at IDR 25 (~Rp542-548bn), a 50% discount to the IDR 50 floor. Stake 5.71% -> 7.59% (87.48bn shares). Disclosed 7 Sep. Stated purpose: investment, "not aimed at control". Seller not disclosed.
Morgan Stanley repo of 7.4bn GOTO shares at IDR 25-27 (not an outright sale)

Repurchase agreement in negotiated market: 1.45bn at IDR 27 + 5.95bn at IDR 25 (~Rp187bn). Reported stake 7.38% -> 6.99%. Widely headlined as a sale, but Kiwoom (Liza Camelia Suryanata) notes it is a repo, holding is indirect/non-controlling and may include client/custodial positions; IDR 25 reflects bilateral pricing/collateral haircut, not a regular-market reference.
Morgan Stanley sells 1.39bn at IDR 29, buys 420m at IDR 28

Net ~973m shares sold. Stake 7.059% -> 6.9745% (81.28bn -> 80.30bn shares). FLAG: IDN Financials reports a separate 997.9m sale on 11 Sep leaving 5.42% - a parallel ~5.4% series likely reflects a different Morgan Stanley reporting entity/account (filings do not reconcile).
Morgan Stanley buys 400m GOTO at IDR 27
~Rp10.8bn; stake 6.9951% -> 7.0299%. Disclosure lists Morgan Stanley & Co International Plc in an organised group with Morgan Stanley & Co LLC - Client Account. Purpose: investment.
Morgan Stanley sells 450m GOTO at IDR 27
Stake 7.0233% -> 6.9842% (80.8bn -> ~80.4bn shares). Executed before the IDR 1 minimum price took effect (28 Sep).
Per IDX >5% holder report dated 25 Sep; trade date and price not stated. Part of the ~5.4% reporting series (see 11 Sep FLAG).
IDX lowers minimum price from IDR 50 to IDR 1; GOTO trades below IDR 50

New IDX rule (applies to Special Monitoring Board/full call auction stocks per source; applicability path to GOTO not verified) effective ~28/29 Sep 2026 (source date inconsistent). GOTO traded ~IDR 37 on 28/29 Sep; Telkomsel's stake (1.99%, cost IDR 270/sh) down ~86%. GOTO top foreign net sell in early Oct 2026.
GoTo letter to IDX explains share-price volatility as technical

Management attributes the fall to: FTSE exit (22 Jun), IDR 50 floor suppressing volume since May, MSCI exit (31 Aug) forcing passive selling that could not clear on the regular market, and the IDR 1 floor (28 Sep) letting queued sellers sell. Says it knows only of trades disclosed on IDX, is unaware of any majority-shareholder transactions (largest holder ~7%), and that the ESOP/MSOP plan for treasury shares was cancelled in favour of capital reduction. "Current share price does not reflect strengthening fundamentals."
Price not stated. A further ~70m-share sale was also reported (IDN Financials, date not captured). Combined outright sales since 23 Sep ~1.4bn shares vs ~13bn GOTO shares traded on 9 Oct alone.
Assessment: was the Sep-Oct 2026 drop caused by Morgan Stanley OTC buying of ESOP shares? - No evidence

(1) No source identifies the sellers to Morgan Stanley; none mentions employees/ESOP/GoTo Peopleverse Fund. Timing (21 Aug-2 Sep, around MSCI exit, Rp152bn net foreign negotiated-market selling at avg IDR 24 on 1 Sep, BlackRock stake down) points to passive index funds exiting. (2) No new ESOP supply: GoTo cancelled the treasury-to-MESOP plan (Jul 2026); only recent ESOP sale found is Deputy CEO 516m at ~IDR 52 in Mar 2026; the "IDR 2" figure is the 2022 exercise price. (3) Main driver: removal of the IDR 50 floor on 28 Sep released pent-up selling; regular price fell 50->43->37->32->28 (25 Sep-1 Oct; auto-reject lower 29 Sep) and converged to the IDR 23-27 negotiated-market level. The OTC trades revealed the clearing price rather than caused the fall. (4) Morgan Stanley outright sales since 23 Sep (~1.4bn shares) are small vs daily volume; 7.4bn on 4 Sep was a repo. Gaps: IDX negotiated-market counterparties and KSEI data not obtained; two Morgan Stanley stake series (~7% vs ~5.4%) do not reconcile.
GOTO falls 10% to Rp27; largest traded value on IDX; foreign net buy ~Rp134bn
Close Rp27 (-10.0%); value Rp773bn, 28.1bn shares. IHSG -2.59% to 5,936. Foreign investors net bought ~Rp133-134bn of GOTO while net selling the market. Stock -46% in a month.
Scheduled EGM: cancel 32,186,417,803 treasury shares (capital reduction) and approve Catherine Hindra's resignation

Record date 21 Sep 2026. Agenda: (1) capital reduction by retiring 32,186,417,803 Series A treasury shares bought 12 Jun 2024 - 11 Jun 2025 (~2.7% of shares) with amendment of Articles; (2) resignation of Deputy President Director. No quasi-reorganization/par value change found.
